title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: When you one-hot encode, each unique item in your data gets its own dimension. For example, if you have $$4$$ unique items, your encoding will have $$4$$ dimensions. Think about how many unique 6-letter combinations can be formed from the DNA letters.

title: Calculating Unique Combinations
text: Consider how many different letters are in the DNA alphabet. Then, think about how many different ways you can arrange these letters in a sequence of $$6$$. This will give you the number of unique 6-letter combinations.

title: Calculate the Number of Unique 6-Letter Combinations
text: How many unique 6-letter combinations can be formed from the DNA letters T, G, C, and A?

title: Connecting to Dimensionality
text: Once you know the number of unique 6-letter combinations, remember that each combination gets its own dimension in one-hot encoding. Multiply the number of combinations by the number of DNA strings to find the total dimensions.
